meta.title: The Frog Under the Shell
meta.textType: story: a traditional tale told by Grandpa

paragraphs: On Sunday, February seventh, Dad took Lily, Tom, and Pip to Grandma and Grandpa's house at Green Hill. After lunch, Grandpa sat on an old chair on the porch. Lily and Tom sat on the steps, and Pip lay on the porch with his red ball. A half coconut shell stood upside down on the rail. Lily told Grandpa about her school, her club, and the blog. "I know everything about our school," she said. Grandpa smiled. "Do you know the frog under the coconut shell?" he asked. "No, I do not," said Lily. "Then listen," said Grandpa.

This was Grandpa's story. A small green frog lived under an old coconut shell next to a deep pond. The shell had a small hole at the top, and the frog looked through it every day. He saw a round piece of blue sky, and he believed that it was the whole sky. Green leaves and gray stones lay all around the shell, and the frog was happy among them. One morning, a white duck swam on the pond. "The sky is wide," said the duck, "and no one has seen all of it." "That is impossible!" said the frog. "The sky is round, and it is right here." The duck dived into the deep water and swam away. The frog did not believe the duck, so he sat in the shade of his shell.

At last, the frog climbed on top of the shell. First, he looked up. The sky was wide and blue, and white clouds floated in it. Then he looked down at the pond. It was big, and the duck swam below him. Beyond the pond, the land was green, and tall trees stood around the water. "Now I can see clearly," said the frog. After that, he laughed at his small shell. "This is wonderful!" he said. Finally, he said, "The world is bigger than my home."

That was the end of Grandpa's story. "Is it true?" asked Tom. "Frogs do not talk, Tom," said Grandpa, and he laughed. "But the idea is true, because no one knows everything." Lily looked at the coconut shell on the rail. She said nothing. Pip put his red ball next to her foot.
That evening, Lily went to Grandpa's shelf in the living room. She took down a big atlas and opened it on the floor. Tom stood in the door and saw it. He smiled, and he said nothing.
text.summary: At Green Hill, Lily says that she knows everything about her school. Grandpa tells her the tale of a small frog who thinks that his coconut shell is the whole sky, and that evening Lily takes an atlas from his shelf.
